newsitem.title: FINLAND: EURO SEEN MAIN EUROPE FORESTRY CURRENCY - FEDERATION.
newsitem.headline: EURO SEEN MAIN EUROPE FORESTRY CURRENCY - FEDERATION.

text.p: The euro is likely to become the main pricing and invoicing currency, replacing the U.S. dollar, in intra-European trade in forest industry products, the Finnish Forest Industries Federation said on Wednesday.

"When economic and monetary union is implemented, the euro will become more popular both as a reserve currency and as a means of payment," federation managing director Matti Korhonen wrote in banking group Merita Oy's quarterly Unitas.
The weight of the euro will reflect the European Union's position in world trade and partly reduce the weight of the dollar, he said according to a Merita statement on his piece.
"In intra-European trade in forest industry products the position of the euro will strengthen," Korhonen added.
In the EMU area, production inputs like wages, raw materials, energy, capital and transport would "soon" be paid in euros, which will make the euro the main invoicing and pricing currency, he said.
Currently, Finnish forest industry companies invoice three quarters of their revenues in EU member countries' currencies and slightly over 17 percent in dollars, Korhonen said.
He said sawn goods, where the Swedish crown is an important invoicing currency, could be a problem for Finnish producers.
If Finland joined EMU and Sweden opted out, it would be "essential" for the Finnish forest industry that EMU countries start denominating European sawn goods trade in euros, he added.

Currently, around 75 percent of European trade in hardwood sawn goods is priced in Swedish crowns and about 25 percent in dollars, Korhonen said. In this respect, the importance of both currencies would diminish if the euro became Europe's main forest industry currency. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
